title: What "learning" means
summary: Adjust numbers to make an error smaller: gradient descent.

cards.title: Learning = reducing an error
cards.body:
When people say a model "learns", they mean something very concrete: it has **numbers** (weights), a way to measure how **wrong** it is (the **loss**), and a rule to nudge the numbers so the loss shrinks.

That rule is almost always **gradient descent**: find which direction is downhill, take a small step, repeat.
Here the "model" has one number, x, and the loss is a simple curve with its lowest point at x = 3.

cards.title: The learning rate
cards.body:
- Too small: training crawls.
- Too big: every step overshoots and training **diverges** (try learning rate 105 in the Algorithm Lab).

Choosing it well is one of the most important practical decisions when training real models.

cards.question: At x = 5 the slope of the loss is +4. Which way does gradient descent move x?
cards.explain: x -= rate × slope. A positive slope means the loss rises to the right, so we step left.
